title: Vacuum Tubes vs Silicon Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav switches on his grandfather's old valve radio and has to wait for the music, while his phone plays instantly. Why? In this animated lesson we look inside a hot cathode to see thermionic emission and the work function (about 4.5 eV for tungsten), then build Fleming's vacuum diode (1904) on a live breadboard: the oscilloscope shows an alternating input turning into one-way current, which is rectification. We add de Forest's grid to make a triode (1906) and list the real problems of tubes.

Then the semiconductor answer: silicon, doping with phosphorus (n-type, free electrons) and boron (p-type, holes), the p-n junction, the depletion layer and its barrier of about 0.7 V for silicon, and forward vs reverse bias with the I-V curve drawn live on the scope. A worked example finds the current through a silicon diode and a 1 kilo-ohm resistor on 5 V (4.3 mA), followed by why semiconductors won, the exam trap (forward bias means p side to plus), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 2 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 1: Introduction to Electronics (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
